title: Standing Stones
lead: Upright stones set up as memorials, witnesses or signs of a god's presence. The patriarchs and Moses set them up, but later law forbade them as Canaanite worship objects (Genesis 28:18; Exodus 24:4; Deuteronomy 16:22).

sections.b: Jacob raises stones at Bethel (Genesis 28:18; 35:14), at Galeed with Laban (31:45–52) and over Rachel's grave (35:20). Moses sets up twelve pillars at Sinai (Exodus 24:4), and Joshua sets stones at the Jordan and at Shechem (Joshua 4:20; 24:26–27). But Israel is told to smash the pillars of Canaan (Exodus 23:24) and not to set up its own (Deuteronomy 16:22), and the prophets attack them (Hosea 10:1–2; Micah 5:13). Isaiah, however, foresees "a pillar to the LORD" at Egypt's border (Isaiah 19:19). Archaeologists have found standing stones at Gezer, Hazor, Arad and many other sites.
